Inside OpenAI’s comeback in coding, from a failed launch to the app that took over ChatGPT  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

HOW CODEX HAPPENED https://every.?ev_audience=free


INSIDE OPENAI’S COMEBACK IN CODING, FROM A FAILED LAUNCH TO THE APP THAT TOOK OVER CHATGPT https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Dan Shipper https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Photoshop/Every illustration.

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



Codex is one of the most important untold stories in the history of technology.

A year ago, OpenAI’s coding effort looked lost in the wilderness:

 * Codex Cloud had flopped.
 * Their $3 billion Windsurf deal fell apart.
 * Claude Code was running away with the market.

Less than 12 months later, a tiny team in the “backwaters” of OpenAI built an app that grew to more than 40 million users, swallowed ChatGPT from the inside, and remade the entire company.

I had a front-row seat to the whole arc—from a conference room in their office the night before GPT-5 launched to the day Codex took over ChatGPT—and spent months interviewing the people who made it happen, including OpenAI’s Greg Brockman and Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux. It’s a wild story about what it takes to build when the frontier is moving beneath your feet:

Read ‘How Codex Happened’ https://every.?ev_audience=free

Your free Every account includes 10 prompts for applying lessons from the story to your own work and the story as a PDF.

The story is also completely agent-native. Paid members get the full transcripts of all six of my interviews with OpenAI insiders, and a live session with me tomorrow about how we reported and wrote the story with Codex and what I learned about how OpenAI came back.

----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Youtube: Muse Wonder: Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XfdIhd1g6EI)

**1/ ****[Muse Wonder and Wonder Full](https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-wonder)** - two new models from Meta. Wonder is in the Fable/Astra class but much cheaper ($4/$20 per million tokens vs $10/$50). Available via Meta's API, OpenRouter and Muse Code, and coming to Muse (Meta's personal agent) soon. Wonder Full is the stronger model, currently only in Muse Code (from $50/mo).

Meta's also introducing Active Memory and Active Focus. Memory lets Muse remember things about you over weeks and months. Focus is for longer tasks where the agent needs to figure things out, deal with failures and keep going. Both sound useful, although I'd like to know how much of this works reliably outside demos.

Zuck and Alexandr Wang went on [Cheeky Pint](https://x.com/collision/status/2109714250226905248) to talk about the models. Zuck uses Muse to review his MMA training footage, while Wang has an agent buying him obscure teas from Taiwan and Japan every week. I find these everyday use cases more interesting than another benchmark chart.

Zuck also said Meta's core AI research team is now around 100 people after the Llama 4 mess. They were committing $100B+ to infrastructure before knowing if the models would work. That's quite a lot of faith in 100 people.

**2/ **[**Microsoft's Maia 300**](https://x.com/satyanadella/status/2109631106404487523) - Microsoft's new AI chip. It claims 40% more AI output than leading Nvidia GPUs for the same power. Built on TSMC's 2nm process, with 96 chips per rack using ~167kW.

Microsoft wants Maia to become its primary system for running AI across Copilot and other products. Multi-gigawatt deployments start in 2027, and [Reuters reports](https://www.reuters.com/business/microsoft-plans-huge-deployment-its-own-ai-chips-with-an-eye-saving-costs-2026-10-12/) it could deploy over 1M chips next year.

Microsoft's spending $175B+ on data centers and equipment this year. At that scale, I'd be trying to make my own chips too :)

I don't think Nvidia's going anywhere, but it's funny that some of its biggest customers are also spending billions trying to buy fewer Nvidia chips. Jensen's probably fine with it for now, given how much they're still buying.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Meta Muse Wonder ](https://x.com/alexandr_wang/status/2109689491300794551?s=20)- a new** **frontier model that keeps track of what matters to you with Active Memory & Active Focus to work towards your goals

* [GLM-Legal](https://x.com/Zai_org/status/2109678174468534511?s=20) - designed for real legal workflows: contract review, evidence analysis, compliance, and more

* [Treg](https://treg.to/people-search) - one skill gives your agent 1B+ contacts across Apollo, Hunter, Tomba, People Data Labs. 111 providers behind one token

* [Claude Dashboards & Motion](https://claude.com/resources/articles/dashboards-and-motion) -** **build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude 

* [SubQ Snap](https://x.com/alex_whedon/status/2109676361371824229?s=20) - the first long-context decision model for real enterprise work

* [Anatomy](https://x.com/wheresryan22/status/2108948624004526516) - describe a machine, get a 3D model you can take apart

* [Grok Bot](https://x.com/i/trending/2108921878865727956) - XAI's agents now have a dedicated email for independent actions. It can also search, read, and monitor X

* [Microsoft-Decision-1](https://commandline.microsoft.com/microsoft-decision-1-model-foundry) - Microsoft's fastest decision-making model yet


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
* [Andrej Karpathy](https://www.tradingview.com/news/benzinga:521fa1515094b:0-former-openai-researcher-issues-grim-warning-says-only-5-000-people-have-access-to-frontier-ai-while-2-billion-use-it-as-better-google-search/?utm_source=www.theneurondaily.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=meta-s-muse-wonder-is-here-priced-like-opus) estimated that only about 5,000 people have internal access to the most advanced AI systems

* [Anthropic's Frontier Red Team](https://x.com/ns123abc/status/2109769030416425222?s=20) believes small AI models may now be months away from being capable of self-replicating without access to a data center

* Patrick Collison on [agents in the economy](https://x.com/patrickc/status/2108706907859116280)

* Muse Wonder: [Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI](https://cheekypint.substack.com/p/muse-wonder-zuckerberg-and-wangs)

* Character.AI [files for bankruptcy](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/characterai-files-bankruptcy-agrees-sell-some-assets-disney-20-million-2026-10-13/), agrees to $20M Disney asset sale

* You can just [vibe-code Beehiiv](https://x.com/marclou/status/2108509543810605218)

* Amazon has over [1 million robot workers](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/inside-amazons-robotic-arms-race-and-what-it-means-for-the-future-of-human-work). What's next for human employees?

* [38 things we've learned](https://newsletter.posthog.com/p/38-things-weve-learned-about-building) about building AI products

* The state of [self-improvement AI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Q1mdn5ZGvM)
